step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents Mahindra Electric's NEMO IoT platform on AWS. Electric vehicles send real-time telemetry over MQTT/TCP IP to an ELB, which load balances traffic to an EC2 broker. The broker pushes the message stream into Amazon Kinesis (retained for 3 days). A Lambda function picks up records from Kinesis for dual processing paths: 1) Urgent alerts (like geofencing alerts) are pushed to SNS to notify Fleet Operators in real-time. 2) Operational and telemetry data is stored in an S3 data lake. AWS Glue scans, transforms, and curates this data (e.g., driver ratings) and writes it back to S3. Amazon Athena then queries this curated S3 data to render dashboard insights and analytics for Fleet Operators.

nodes.notes: EC2 instance running an MQTT/TCP broker.

nodes.name: Kinesis
nodes.notes: Data stream retaining telemetry payloads for up to 3 days.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Processes Kinesis events; splits immediate alerts from long-term storage.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Notification service delivering critical vehicle alerts.

nodes.name: Fleet OP
nodes.notes: Fleet operators monitoring real-time notifications and fleet insights.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Single source of truth data lake holding terabytes of telemetry data.

nodes.name: Glue
nodes.notes: Scans, curates, and transforms raw data (e.g. driver rating algorithms).

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Interactive query engine driving operational dashboards.
